title: Intravitreal anti-VEGF injection
subtitle: Asepsis, pars plana injection and a perfusion check

sources.org: Avery RL et al. Retina 34 Suppl 12:S1
sources.title: Intravitreal injection technique and monitoring: updated guidelines of an expert panel

indications: Diabetic macular oedema and proliferative diabetic retinopathy (selected).
Macular oedema from retinal vein occlusion; myopic choroidal neovascularisation; other indications per protocol.
contraindications: Active ocular or periocular infection (blepharitis with discharge, conjunctivitis).
preparation: Confirm the indication, drug and dose from the treatment plan and today's imaging; check the eye.
Check recent cardiovascular events per drug guidance; check pregnancy where relevant.
Consent: endophthalmitis (rare but sight-threatening), raised pressure, retinal tear or detachment, cataract from lens touch, subconjunctival haemorrhage, floaters.
positioning: Supine or reclined with the head supported and the eye looking slightly away from the injection site.
equipment: Lid speculum, povidone-iodine 5%, topical anaesthetic, the drug in a prefilled syringe or drawn up with a filter needle, a 30G needle, calipers, sterile cotton buds.
anatomy: The pars plana, about 3.5 to 4 mm behind the limbus, is between the ciliary body in front and the retina behind: entering there avoids both the lens and the retina.
criticalSafety: Right patient, right eye, right drug.
Povidone-iodine 5% and no lash contact with the needle.
Check the optic disc is perfused afterwards.
commonErrors: Injecting through the limbus or too far back.
Not checking perfusion in a glaucomatous eye.
complications: Raised pressure and central retinal artery occlusion.
Lens injury, retinal tear or detachment.
postop: Usually no pad; lubricants as needed.
Same-day return for increasing pain, redness or falling vision in the days after.
Next injection and review per the treatment protocol.

steps.emphasis: Confirm the eye against the treatment plan; patients with bilateral disease are a wrong-eye risk.
Read the patient, eye, drug, dose and batch aloud.
Topical drops, with a pledget or subconjunctival local if preferred.
Supine or reclined, head supported, the eye looking away from the injection quadrant.
Povidone-iodine 5% to the conjunctiva and the injection site, and to the lid margins; masks or no talking to limit droplets.
A speculum keeps lashes and lid margins away from the needle.
Explain the endophthalmitis warning signs for the coming days and give the emergency number.

step.ivi.site.title: Choosing and marking the injection site
step.ivi.site.why: The pars plana window is narrow: too anterior hits the ciliary body or lens, too posterior risks the retina.
how: Measure 3.5 to 4 mm from the limbus with calipers (3.5 mm in pseudophakic eyes, 4 mm in phakic eyes), usually inferotemporal.
Reapply povidone-iodine to the marked site.

step.ivi.inject.title: Injecting the drug
step.ivi.inject.why: A controlled, slow injection with the needle aimed at the centre of the globe avoids the lens and the retina and limits reflux.
how: Steady the globe; insert the 30G needle perpendicular to the sclera, aimed towards the centre of the eye.
Inject the dose slowly, withdraw the needle, and press the site briefly with a sterile cotton bud to limit reflux.
pitfalls: Aiming towards the lens in a phakic eye.
Touching the needle to the lashes or lids.

step.ivi.perfusion.title: Perfusion and pressure check
step.ivi.perfusion.why: The injected volume raises the eye pressure briefly; in a glaucomatous eye it can stop the central retinal artery. A quick check of vision and the optic disc finds this before the patient leaves.
how: Ask the patient to count fingers or see hand movements, or look at the optic disc for perfusion.
Measure the pressure if vision is poor or the eye has glaucoma.
If the artery is not perfused, lower the pressure (anterior chamber paracentesis by a trained doctor, pressure-lowering drugs) and recheck.
structuresAtRisk: Optic nerve and central retinal artery
pitfalls: Sending the patient home without checking vision.
